answer: Each agent must forge an epoch-locked state root before trading: a Blake3 hash over a dedicated 64 GB RAM array seeded by its identity key, published on-chain. Verifiers re-derive a random 1 GB slice within 30 seconds and compare hashes; any mismatch freezes the account and slashes its $500 bond. A quill of cheap identities cannot share one array, since each root binds to a distinct memory layout, like light through a prism splitting apart. One honest agent holds 64 GB; 10 fakes must hold 640 GB of RAM, turning identity farming into a hardware bill, not a copy-paste trick.
